walkthroughs.body_html:
Galaxies & Cosmology — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Galaxies & Cosmology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Galaxies & Cosmology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the cosmic microwave background?
options: Infinite.
Light from the most distant galaxies.
Background noise from human microwave ovens.
Relic radiation from when the universe became transparent, about 380,000 years after the Big Bang.

mcqs.q: What is the current best estimate for the age of the universe?
options: Infinite.
About 13.8 billion years.
About 6,000 years.
How far it can see.

mcqs.q: What does a telescope's aperture primarily determine?
options: How far it can see.
Infinite.
Magnification.
Light-gathering ability and angular resolution.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Steady-state model”?
options: Discredited rival model (Hoyle, Bondi, Gold 1948) where the universe is unchanging on large scales.
Cosmological model: universe expanded from a hot, dense state ~13.8 Gyr ago.
Brief phase (10^-36 to 10^-32 s) of exponential expansion that smoothed and flattened the universe.
Primordial production of light nuclei (H, He, Li) in the first ~3 minutes.
